title: Qt: add command line options support in the TLS Keylog Launcher
description:
Add support for command line parameters, rename the preference to match.
Use the correct `SSLKEYLOGFILE` environment variable name in the text.
Rename SSL to TLS, we are no longer in 1999. Clarify that applications
other than browsers can be selected. Various dialog text improvements.
Move the Launch button to the right to make it stand out more.

Relates to #19471
___
I am targetting the 4.2 release for this given that this should address some confusion on what this dialog is doing.

After the changes, the dialog looks like this:

![image](/uploads/f4a8593e048b0be6b5918f8eb48d4c82/image.png){width=50%}

This screenshot covers the following:
1. The keylog file is set to `/tmp/tls.keys`.
2. The command line is set to Chrome to demonstrate handling of spaces in the program path:
```sh
"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --user-data-dir=/tmp/cr --no-first-run --disable-background-networking
```
3. I hit the save button, and start the packet capture on the `utun0` interface for `host example.com`.
4. I hit the Launch button, start Chrome in a new profile, and visit https://example.com

notes.body: requested review from @geraldcombs, @jvalverde, and @johnthacker

Open questions:
1. Should `browser_tlskeylog.path` be renamed to `tlskeylog_launcher_path` or something similar?
2. The dialog title in `ui/qt/tlskeylog_launcher_dialog.cpp` is still `Web Browser`. Should that be changed to `Program path` or similar?
3. In general, should more be done to clarify that the option specifies a path to a program instead of a command line string? Or should we change this to accept command line parameters, e.g. `chromium --user-data-dir=/tmp/cr`?

Personally I think that this dialog is not really useful, except for the simplest cases. Usually you should specify some command line arguments like `firefox -profile /tmp/ff` or `chromium --user-data-dir --no-first-run --disable-background-networking --user-data-dir=/tmp/cr/` to reduce the capture size.
mentioned in merge request !13143
mentioned in issue #19471

I agree with both the idea and trying to target 4.2, because we haven't made an official release with the preference so hopefully that means not having to mark the name with "ssl" as obsolete and read the value from the old one. It has been in a release candidate, but IMHO that's an acceptable breakage.

There were other suggestions in #19471, in particular:

- Change from a single program to a command line that accepts arguments (also raised in the above thread).
- Link to documentation that explains how to run browsers in a separate profile.
- Track executed processes and offer a terminate button.

I think that the above improvements could be done as incremental changes on top of the current editorial fix to make some progress. We should however address the preference name before the final 4.2 release I think. Right now it is `browser_tlskeylog.path`, should it become `tlskeylog_command` or something similarly future-proof?
`tlskeylog_command` sounds fine to me.

splitCommand was introduced in Qt5.15, however we still support Qt5.12

You're right, https://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qprocess.html#splitCommand

While the current behavior of escaping a quote with triple quotes might feel familiar to someone on Windows, this is not the case for other platforms. I will have a look at possible alternatives. Suggestions are welcome!

Edit: so in theory we can use [`g_shell_parse_argv`](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/func.shell_parse_argv.html), except that it will not have the desired behavior on Windows due to unescaping backslashes.
Please try !13237, does it address your build issue?

!13237 works fine

for the edit, there is `g_shell_unqoute()` if that fills the need?

Ok, thanks for testing!

`g_shell_unquote` won't help, it would also turn `C:\Program Files` into `C:Program Files`. That's why I am sticking to the current implementation for now, it preserves most characters.

> escaping a quote with triple quotes might feel familiar to someone on Windows,

Actually no, it looks very awkward to me. But I hardly use `cmd /c` and to launch a GUI app the `start` command is the one to use.

The example at https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/19471#note_1645488554 using triple quotes does not work -- it opens a new tab in an existing browser window, thus the SSLKEYLOGFILE is not picked up. This form does work:

`cmd /c start "" "%ProgramFiles%/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe" --user-data-dir="%TEMP%\cr" --no-first-run --disable-background-networking https://wireshark.org`

Windows has a native [ExpandEnvironmentStrings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/windows/win32/api/processenv/nf-processenv-expandenvironmentstringsa) function to expand environment variables. Calling this before `QProcess::splitCommand` will do the trick.

Note: Windows accepts both forward-slash and backslash in pathnames.

Clearly I have been away from Windows usage for too long, you are probably right that it should have been `cmd /c start` :sweat_smile: 

I am not sure what is going to break if I unconditionally convert all backwards slashes to forward slashes on Windows.

Expanding every variable after word-splitting should be doable, but it would still not provide the full shell functionality.

For example, on Windows, perhaps we want to support both the usual and Powershell forms:

    "%ProgramFiles%/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe" --user-data-dir="%TEMP%\cr"
    "$Env:ProgramFiles/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe" --user-data-dir="$Env:TEMP\cr"

and on Linux, perhaps this:

    firefox -profile $TMPDIR/ff
    firefox -profile ${TMPDIR}/ff

but what if someone wants to have more shell functionality, and ends up doing this:

    sh -c "mkdir -p $TMPDIR/ff && firefox -profile $TMPDIR/ff"

if `$TMPDIR` contains spaces, and Wireshark would expand this, then we have a problem. So that's why I am tempted to maintain the current situation where we do not touch the arguments except when needed for word splitting.

If it turns out that I am wrong with this based on more user's feedback, it could be changed later again.

I agree you have to draw the line somewhere. For _full_ shell features I would say use a script for that (and call that) and keep it simple here. My intention for basic support for environment variables is that it allows for generic solutions and makes it possible to use examples in the documentation that actually works. The [ExpandEnvironmentStrings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/windows/win32/api/processenv/nf-processenv-expandenvironmentstringsa) Windows function, I mentioned earlier, also does just a limited expansion compared to what `cmd` can do. IMO that's good enough and then there is no need to wrap the command line in a `cmd` command. For Linux [wordexp](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/wordexp.3.html) does a similar job (to avoid `sh)`. Regarding possible spaces in paths, you can use double quotes as usual when the command line itself is a single-quoted string. E.g.: `bash -c 'firefox -profile "$TMPDIR"/ff &'` But the triple quotes are still needed by [QProcess::splitCommand](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qprocess.html#splitCommand) for a quote character itself: > Tokens with spaces can be surrounded by double quotes; three consecutive double quotes represent the quote character itself.

commits_data.message:
Qt: add command line options support in the TLS Keylog Launcher

Add support for command line parameters, rename the preference to match.
Use the correct `SSLKEYLOGFILE` environment variable name in the text.
Rename SSL to TLS, we are no longer in 1999. Clarify that applications
other than browsers can be selected. Various dialog text improvements.
Move the Launch button to the right to make it stand out more.

Relates to #19471
